data.title: Two dates between the pages

memoryNodes.cue: Two writers give different accounts of the same life.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 两位写作者从不同角度写同一个人的生活。

memoryNodes.cue: Lin keeps both dates and adds clear labels.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 林保留两个日期并补上清楚标签。

memoryNodes.object: the date card between the books
memoryNodes.location: the date card between the books
memoryNodes.cue: The card marks the pages they need to check.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 日期卡标出需要核对的书页。

data.situation:
At two o’clock that Wednesday, Maya found a biography of Rowe on the adjacent shelf. Lin picked up the writer’s autobiography, hoping to hear the same events in her own voice. They carried both books to the low table at the end of the aisle. One introduction dated Rowe’s first story in a national magazine to 1976; the other mentioned a piece printed in 1974. Lin began a timeline on a loose sheet, then stopped before moving either date. The wording mattered. The earlier piece had appeared in a local workshop booklet, while 1976 marked her first publication in a national magazine. Once they had clarified the chronology, Maya placed the two events in chronological order. A date card from the librarian stayed between the open books so they could find the pages again. Maya: The biography dates her first story in a national magazine to 1976, but her autobiography mentions a booklet from 1974. Is one of them wrong?
Lin: Not necessarily. “First in a workshop booklet” and “first in a national magazine” are different.
Maya: So the timeline needs two labels, not one corrected date.
Lin: Yes. Let’s keep the page numbers with them. We may need these details when we introduce the writer.

readingBlocks.en: At two o’clock that Wednesday, Maya found a biography of Rowe on the adjacent shelf. Lin picked up the writer’s autobiography, hoping to hear the same events in her own voice. They carried both books to the low table at the end of the aisle. One introduction dated Rowe’s first story in a national magazine to 1976; the other mentioned a piece printed in 1974. Lin began a timeline on a loose sheet, then stopped before moving either date. The wording mattered. The earlier piece had appeared in a local workshop booklet, while 1976 marked her first publication in a national magazine. Once they had clarified the chronology, Maya placed the two events in chronological order. A date card from the librarian stayed between the open books so they could find the pages again.
readingBlocks.zh: 那天星期三，两点钟，玛雅在相邻书架找到一本罗的传记。林拿起了作者的自传，想听她本人怎样讲述同一段经历。他们把两本书带到过道尽头的矮桌。一篇介绍说，罗第一次在全国性杂志发表故事是在1976年；另一篇却提到了1974年印出的一篇作品。林开始在散页上画时间线，却没有急着移动任何一个日期。区别在于具体说法：较早的作品印在地方工作坊的小册子里，1976年则是她的作品首次登上全国性杂志。厘清事件先后后，玛雅把两件事按时间顺序排列。图书管理员给的日期卡夹在两本摊开的书之间，方便她们再次找到那几页。

readingBlocks.en:
Maya: The biography dates her first story in a national magazine to 1976, but her autobiography mentions a booklet from 1974. Is one of them wrong?
Lin: Not necessarily. “First in a workshop booklet” and “first in a national magazine” are different.
Maya: So the timeline needs two labels, not one corrected date.
Lin: Yes. Let’s keep the page numbers with them. We may need these details when we introduce the writer.
readingBlocks.zh:
玛雅：传记说她第一次在全国性杂志发表故事是在1976年，可自传提到了1974年的小册子。是不是有一本写错了？
林：未必。“第一次印在工作坊小册子里”和“第一次登上全国性杂志”不是一回事。
玛雅：那时间线应该写两个标签，而不是改掉一个日期。
林：对。页码也一起记下来。介绍作者时，也许用得上这些细节。

glossary.note: a biography of someone；记录对象不是书的作者本人，自传另区分。
glossary.example: Maya found a biography of Rowe on the adjacent shelf.
glossary.exampleZh: 玛雅在相邻书架找到一本罗的传记。

externalEvidence.definition: an account of the series of events making up a person's life

glossary.note: writer’s autobiography为作者自述；不保证和别人的记述完全一致，仍需核措辞。
glossary.example: Lin picked up the writer’s autobiography, hoping to hear the same events in her own voice.
glossary.exampleZh: 林拿起作者的自传，想听她本人怎样讲述同一段经历。

glossary.zh: 按事件先后顺序排列的
glossary.note: chronological形容词修饰order；源Chinese_Meaning填英文定义原样保留。
glossary.example: Maya placed the two events in chronological order.
glossary.exampleZh: 玛雅把两件事按时间顺序排列。

externalEvidence.definition: relating to or arranged according to temporal order

glossary.note: chronology这里指两件事的发生顺序，不是年代测定技术或一本独立编年史。
glossary.example: Once they had clarified the chronology, Maya placed the two events in chronological order.
glossary.exampleZh: 厘清事件先后后，玛雅把两件事按时间顺序排列。

externalEvidence.definition: an arrangement of events in time

glossary.note: a timeline可数名词，是图形列示时间与事件；原timelines为复数，共用身份。
glossary.example: Lin began a timeline on a loose sheet, then stopped before moving either date.
glossary.exampleZh: 林开始在散页上画时间线，却没有急着移动任何一个日期。

externalEvidence.definition: a sequence of related events arranged in chronological order and displayed along a line (usually drawn left to right or top to bottom)

retrievalPrompts.cue: You want to hear the writer describe her own life. Explain which of the two books you would choose.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 你想听作者本人讲自己的经历，该选她的自传还是别人写的传记？说说理由。
acceptableAnswers: I would choose her autobiography because I want to read her own account, rather than someone else’s biography of her.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Two accounts mention 1974 and 1976. Explain why you would check what each date refers to before changing either one.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 两个材料分别写1974和1976，你会怎样说明为什么先不改日期？
acceptableAnswers: We need to clarify the chronology: the story appeared in a workshop booklet in 1974, and her first publication in a national magazine was in 1976.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Tell a classmate how you will draw and arrange the two events.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 你想把这两件事画给同学看，怎样说明你打算怎么排？
acceptableAnswers: I will draw a timeline and put the events in chronological order.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法

transferPrompt.cue: You are preparing to talk about a family member’s life. Explain how you will organise the dates without confusing different events.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 换成准备介绍家人的经历，你会怎样组织照片和日期，又避免把两种事件当作矛盾？
acceptableAnswers: I would use a timeline with a separate label for each event, then check the chronology before speaking.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法
